title: Minimax Risk for Causal Targets from Calibrated Marked-Poisson Death Counts
banked_reason: Sound mathematics and verified citations, but achieved incremental novelty below the field floor: paper_score_ceiling 5.2 < 7.4; optimized mark premium and unequal study–audit tradeoff remain open.
gap_reasons: The delivered transfer, certification, count-fiber radius and matching large-information count limit constitute a specialized extension of inherited Poisson decision machinery, with the aggregation geometry obtained from linear programs on independent polynomial coefficient boxes. The finite-information frontier consists of a sufficient strict-gap region, a sequential certificate test and an abstract least-favorable-prior criterion; it does not resolve the optimized mark premium or the study–audit information tradeoff across the benchmark box. Generic loss from temporal aggregation already appears in [Borchers et al. (2014)](https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/2041-210X.12196), leaving the contribution concentrated in this calibrated causal benchmark. The evaluated evidence supplies a tight unit-information full-risk enclosure and high-information comparisons, but no joint full/count precision analysis at modest, unequal information levels that establishes the benchmark's proposed planning value. These substantive limits constrain the projected paper score after editorial repair; the framing does not falsely assert universal strictness or a necessary finite-information threshold. proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived a class-level calibrated marked-Poisson transfer/certification package, including count-fiber radius and rank test, an all-rule count lower bound with matching large-information limit, vanishing full-mark risk, and finite strict-gap and unit-information certificates. The mathematics passed and all seven foundational citations were source-attested, but optimized finite-information mark-premium and unequal study–audit allocation geometry remain open; a certified 4×4 solver would be new research rather than a bounded repair that clears field. Formalization was not entered; no Lean proof or substrate promotion is claimed.
tldr: A finite-dimensional class of one-way calibrated marked-Poisson causal experiments admits a total certified minimax squared-risk algorithm and original-record attaining decisions. A rational linear program computes the causal variation invisible to process totals. Its squared half-diameter is an irreducible count-only risk floor and the exact count minimax limit as study and audit information grow; full marks admit a uniform bound tending to zero. An exact rank test identifies a positive floor and supplies a computable sufficient finite-information threshold for a strict mark-value gap. The mortality lost-time experiment, with its entire five-dimensional box and unknown shared reporting scale, is a concrete corollary. The open content is the optimized finite-information precision and gap geometry. Poisson approximation, finite decision certification, and risk transfer are inherited machinery.
gap: Fixed-channel cause-correction normal theory propagates calibration uncertainty but does not give a target-specific aggregation-risk frontier in a finite-information one-way channel. Generic detection-time insufficiency does not quantify the causal target variation erased by counts or its all-rule minimax cost.
fill: A class-level finite certification and attainment theorem is joined to an exactly computable aggregation floor, a matching large-information count limit, and a primitive rank condition with a finite strict-gap threshold. The fixed mortality box illustrates the frontier and calibrates cause-specific lost-time precision; it is not the sole theorem domain.
